claim: Extracellular Hedgehog (Hh) proteins induce transcriptional changes in target cells by inhibiting the proteolytic processing of full-length Drosophila Ci or mammalian Gli proteins to nuclear transcriptional repressors.
source: Extracellular Hedgehog (Hh) proteins induce transcriptional changes in target cells by inhibiting the proteolytic processing of full-length Drosophila Ci or mammalian Gli proteins to nuclear transcriptional repressors and by activating the full-length Ci or Gli proteins.
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge about Hh signaling mechanisms, presented as background in the abstract.

claim: Extracellular Hedgehog (Hh) proteins induce transcriptional changes in target cells by activating the full-length Ci or Gli proteins.
source: Extracellular Hedgehog (Hh) proteins induce transcriptional changes in target cells by inhibiting the proteolytic processing of full-length Drosophila Ci or mammalian Gli proteins to nuclear transcriptional repressors and by activating the full-length Ci or Gli proteins.
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge about Hh signaling mechanisms, presented as background in the abstract.

claim: Ci variants that cannot be processed supported a normal pattern of graded target gene activation when supplemented by constitutive Ci repressor.
source: Ci variants that cannot be processed supported a normal pattern of graded target gene activation and the development of adults with normal wing morphology, when supplemented by constitutive Ci repressor, showing that Hh can signal normally in the absence of regulated processing.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the study, supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Ci variants that cannot be processed supported the development of adults with normal wing morphology when supplemented by constitutive Ci repressor.
source: Ci variants that cannot be processed supported a normal pattern of graded target gene activation and the development of adults with normal wing morphology, when supplemented by constitutive Ci repressor, showing that Hh can signal normally in the absence of regulated processing.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the study, supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Hh can signal normally in the absence of regulated Ci processing.
source: Ci variants that cannot be processed supported a normal pattern of graded target gene activation and the development of adults with normal wing morphology, when supplemented by constitutive Ci repressor, showing that Hh can signal normally in the absence of regulated processing.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data showing normal signaling with processing-resistant Ci variants.

claim: Processing-resistant Ci variants were significantly activated in the absence of Hh by elimination of Cos2.
source: The processing-resistant Ci variants were also significantly activated in the absence of Hh by elimination of Cos2, likely acting through binding the CORD domain of Ci, or PKA, revealing separate inhibitory roles of these two components in addition to their well-established roles in promoting Ci processing.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the study, supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Processing-resistant Ci variants were significantly activated in the absence of Hh by elimination of PKA.
source: The processing-resistant Ci variants were also significantly activated in the absence of Hh by elimination of Cos2, likely acting through binding the CORD domain of Ci, or PKA, revealing separate inhibitory roles of these two components in addition to their well-established roles in promoting Ci processing.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the study, supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Cos2 likely acts through binding the CORD domain of Ci to inhibit Ci activity.
source: The processing-resistant Ci variants were also significantly activated in the absence of Hh by elimination of Cos2, likely acting through binding the CORD domain of Ci, or PKA, revealing separate inhibitory roles of these two components in addition to their well-established roles in promoting Ci processing.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental data showing that deletion of the CORD domain affects Ci activity in specific ways.

claim: Cos2 and PKA have separate inhibitory roles in addition to their well-established roles in promoting Ci processing.
source: The processing-resistant Ci variants were also significantly activated in the absence of Hh by elimination of Cos2, likely acting through binding the CORD domain of Ci, or PKA, revealing separate inhibitory roles of these two components in addition to their well-established roles in promoting Ci processing.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental data showing activation of processing-resistant Ci variants by elimination of Cos2 or PKA.

claim: Aberrant Hh protein production, distribution, and responses are common causes of developmental birth defects and cancer.
source: Aberrant Hh protein production, distribution, and responses are common causes of developmental birth defects and cancer, including holoprosencephaly, limb and digit abnormalities, medulloblastoma, and basal cell carcinoma (Anderson et al., 2012; Cortes et al., 2019; Ng and Curran, 2011; Pak and Segal, 2016; Petrova and Joyner, 2014; Sasai et al., 2019).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to published literature.

claim: Aberrant Hh signaling causes holoprosencephaly.
source: Aberrant Hh protein production, distribution, and responses are common causes of developmental birth defects and cancer, including holoprosencephaly, limb and digit abnormalities, medulloblastoma, and basal cell carcinoma (Anderson et al., 2012; Cortes et al., 2019; Ng and Curran, 2011; Pak and Segal, 2016; Petrova and Joyner, 2014; Sasai et al., 2019).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to published literature.

claim: Aberrant Hh signaling causes limb and digit abnormalities.
source: Aberrant Hh protein production, distribution, and responses are common causes of developmental birth defects and cancer, including holoprosencephaly, limb and digit abnormalities, medulloblastoma, and basal cell carcinoma (Anderson et al., 2012; Cortes et al., 2019; Ng and Curran, 2011; Pak and Segal, 2016; Petrova and Joyner, 2014; Sasai et al., 2019).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to published literature.

claim: Aberrant Hh signaling causes medulloblastoma.
source: Aberrant Hh protein production, distribution, and responses are common causes of developmental birth defects and cancer, including holoprosencephaly, limb and digit abnormalities, medulloblastoma, and basal cell carcinoma (Anderson et al., 2012; Cortes et al., 2019; Ng and Curran, 2011; Pak and Segal, 2016; Petrova and Joyner, 2014; Sasai et al., 2019).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to published literature.

claim: Aberrant Hh signaling causes basal cell carcinoma.
source: Aberrant Hh protein production, distribution, and responses are common causes of developmental birth defects and cancer, including holoprosencephaly, limb and digit abnormalities, medulloblastoma, and basal cell carcinoma (Anderson et al., 2012; Cortes et al., 2019; Ng and Curran, 2011; Pak and Segal, 2016; Petrova and Joyner, 2014; Sasai et al., 2019).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to published literature.

claim: Many conserved Hh components were initially identified in Drosophila melanogaster and then found to have a mammalian ortholog.
source: Many conserved Hh components were initially identified in Drosophila melanogaster and then found to have a mammalian ortholog, including the key transducing protein Smoothened (Smo), which is now the target of several anticancer drugs (Cortes et al., 2019; Ng and Curran, 2011; Pak and Segal, 2016).
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge about the history of Hh pathway research, supported by citations.

claim: Smoothened (Smo) is now the target of several anticancer drugs.
source: Many conserved Hh components were initially identified in Drosophila melanogaster and then found to have a mammalian ortholog, including the key transducing protein Smoothened (Smo), which is now the target of several anticancer drugs (Cortes et al., 2019; Ng and Curran, 2011; Pak and Segal, 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to published literature.

claim: There are differences between Drosophila and mammalian Hh signal transduction.
source: There are also differences between Drosophila and mammalian Hh signal transduction but neither pathway is fully understood (Briscoe and Thérond, 2013; Huangfu and Anderson, 2006; Kong et al., 2019; Lee et al., 2016; Liu, 2019).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to published literature.

claim: Neither Drosophila nor mammalian Hh signal transduction pathways are fully understood.
source: There are also differences between Drosophila and mammalian Hh signal transduction but neither pathway is fully understood (Briscoe and Thérond, 2013; Huangfu and Anderson, 2006; Kong et al., 2019; Lee et al., 2016; Liu, 2019).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to published literature.

claim: Hh alters the interactions among a set of core signaling components to elicit the transcriptional induction and de-repression of Hh target genes through Cubitus Interruptus (Ci).
source: In flies, Hh alters the interactions among a set of core signaling components to elicit the transcriptional induction and de-repression of Hh target genes through Cubitus Interruptus (Ci), the singular transcription factor of the pathway (Domínguez et al., 1996; Méthot and Basler, 2001; Xiong et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to published literature.

claim: Ci is the singular transcription factor of the Hh pathway in flies.
source: In flies, Hh alters the interactions among a set of core signaling components to elicit the transcriptional induction and de-repression of Hh target genes through Cubitus Interruptus (Ci), the singular transcription factor of the pathway (Domínguez et al., 1996; Méthot and Basler, 2001; Xiong et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to published literature.

claim: Hh can act as a morphogen that signals through Ci to transcribe different Hh target gene products depending on how much ligand is present at the cell membrane.
source: Notably, Hh can act as a morphogen that signals through Ci to transcribe different Hh target gene products depending on how much ligand is present at the cell membrane.
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge about Hh morphogen activity.

claim: In third instar larval Drosophila wing discs, Hh is expressed in posterior compartment cells.
source: In third instar larval Drosophila wing discs, Hh is expressed in posterior compartment cells and Ci is expressed only in anterior cells, so that Hh signals to a band of anterior cells at the anterior-posterior (AP) border with declining strength from posterior to anterior (Blair, 2003; Lawrence and Struhl, 1996).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: In third instar larval Drosophila wing discs, Ci is expressed only in anterior cells.
source: In third instar larval Drosophila wing discs, Hh is expressed in posterior compartment cells and Ci is expressed only in anterior cells, so that Hh signals to a band of anterior cells at the anterior-posterior (AP) border with declining strength from posterior to anterior (Blair, 2003; Lawrence and Struhl, 1996).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Hh signals to a band of anterior cells at the anterior-posterior (AP) border with declining strength from posterior to anterior.
source: In third instar larval Drosophila wing discs, Hh is expressed in posterior compartment cells and Ci is expressed only in anterior cells, so that Hh signals to a band of anterior cells at the anterior-posterior (AP) border with declining strength from posterior to anterior (Blair, 2003; Lawrence and Struhl, 1996).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Ci induces decapentaplegic (dpp) in a broad region at the AP border.
source: Within this AP border territory, Ci induces decapentaplegic (dpp) in a broad region, patched (ptc or a ptc-lacZ transcriptional reporter) in a gradient within a narrower domain, and engrailed (en) only in the cells closest to the source of Hh (see Figure 8; Blair, 2003; Vervoort, 2000).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to published literature and reference to Figure 8.

claim: Ci induces patched (ptc) in a gradient within a narrower domain at the AP border.
source: Within this AP border territory, Ci induces decapentaplegic (dpp) in a broad region, patched (ptc or a ptc-lacZ transcriptional reporter) in a gradient within a narrower domain, and engrailed (en) only in the cells closest to the source of Hh (see Figure 8; Blair, 2003; Vervoort, 2000).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to published literature and reference to Figure 8.

claim: Ci induces engrailed (en) only in the cells closest to the source of Hh.
source: Within this AP border territory, Ci induces decapentaplegic (dpp) in a broad region, patched (ptc or a ptc-lacZ transcriptional reporter) in a gradient within a narrower domain, and engrailed (en) only in the cells closest to the source of Hh (see Figure 8; Blair, 2003; Vervoort, 2000).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to published literature and reference to Figure 8.

claim: Hh controls Ci activity by regulating the processing, activation, and degradation of full-length Ci (Ci-155).
source: Hh controls Ci activity by regulating the processing, activation, and degradation of full-length Ci (known as Ci-155).
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge about Hh regulation of Ci.

claim: In the absence of Hh, the ligand-free receptor Patched (Ptc) actively inhibits the actions of Smoothened (Smo).
source: In the absence of Hh, the ligand-free receptor, Patched (Ptc), actively inhibits the actions of another transmembrane protein Smoothened (Smo), which is present under these conditions at relatively low levels and mainly associated with internal vesicles (Denef et al., 2000; Nakano et al., 2004; Strigini and Cohen, 1997; Zhao et al., 2007).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to published literature.

claim: In the absence of Hh, Smo is present at relatively low levels and mainly associated with internal vesicles.
source: In the absence of Hh, the ligand-free receptor, Patched (Ptc), actively inhibits the actions of another transmembrane protein Smoothened (Smo), which is present under these conditions at relatively low levels and mainly associated with internal vesicles (Denef et al., 2000; Nakano et al., 2004; Strigini and Cohen, 1997; Zhao et al., 2007).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to published literature.

claim: Costal2 (Cos2) acts as a scaffold to bring Protein Kinase A (PKA), Glycogen Synthase Kinase-3 (GSK3), and Casein Kinase-1 (CK1) to Ci-155.
source: Costal2 (Cos2), a kinesin-family protein, complexed to Fused (Fu), acts as a scaffold to bring Protein Kinase A (PKA), Glycogen Synthase Kinase-3 (GSK3), and Casein Kinase-1 (CK1) to C-155 and facilitate phosphorylation of Ci-155 at a series of clustered PKA, CK1 and GSK3 sites (Ranieri et al., 2014; Zhang et al., 2005).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Cos2 facilitates phosphorylation of Ci-155 at a series of clustered PKA, CK1 and GSK3 sites.
source: Costal2 (Cos2), a kinesin-family protein, complexed to Fused (Fu), acts as a scaffold to bring Protein Kinase A (PKA), Glycogen Synthase Kinase-3 (GSK3), and Casein Kinase-1 (CK1) to C-155 and facilitate phosphorylation of Ci-155 at a series of clustered PKA, CK1 and GSK3 sites (Ranieri et al., 2014; Zhang et al., 2005).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Phosphorylation of Ci-155 creates a binding site for Slimb, the substrate recognition component of a Cul1-SCF ubiquitin ligase complex.
source: This creates a binding site for Slimb, the substrate recognition component of a Cul1-SCF ubiquitin ligase complex, which promotes Ci-155 ubiquitination and subsequent partial proteolysis ('processing') by the proteasome to a repressor form (Ci-75).
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge about Ci processing mechanisms.

claim: Slimb promotes Ci-155 ubiquitination and subsequent partial proteolysis by the proteasome to a repressor form (Ci-75).
source: This creates a binding site for Slimb, the substrate recognition component of a Cul1-SCF ubiquitin ligase complex, which promotes Ci-155 ubiquitination and subsequent partial proteolysis ('processing') by the proteasome to a repressor form (Ci-75).
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge about Ci processing mechanisms.

claim: Ci-75 lacks the C-terminal half of Ci-155, which includes its transcriptional activation domain.
source: Ci-75 lacks the C-terminal half of Ci-155, which includes its transcriptional activation domain and an epitope for a monoclonal antibody (2A1) commonly used to detect full-length Ci-155 (Aza-Blanc et al., 1997; Jia et al., 2005; Jiang, 2006; Smelkinson and Kalderon, 2006; Smelkinson et al., 2007).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to published literature.

claim: Ci-75 has a critical role in anterior wing disc cells, silencing transcription of dpp and hh.
source: Ci-75 has a critical role in anterior wing disc cells, silencing transcription of dpp and hh (Domínguez et al., 1996).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: Hh binding to Ptc leads to Smo activation in a process that involves Smo phosphorylation by PKA, CK1, and G-protein-coupled receptor kinase 2 (Gprk2).
source: Hh binding to Ptc leads to Smo activation in a process that involves Smo phosphorylation by PKA, CK1, and G-protein-coupled receptor kinase 2 (Gprk2), Smo accumulation at the plasma membrane and a change in Smo conformation or oligomerization (Kalderon, 2008; Maier et al., 2014; Zhao et al., 2007).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to published literature.

claim: Hh binding to Ptc leads to Smo accumulation at the plasma membrane.
source: Hh binding to Ptc leads to Smo activation in a process that involves Smo phosphorylation by PKA, CK1, and G-protein-coupled receptor kinase 2 (Gprk2), Smo accumulation at the plasma membrane and a change in Smo conformation or oligomerization (Kalderon, 2008; Maier et al., 2014; Zhao et al., 2007).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to published literature.

claim: Hh binding to Ptc leads to a change in Smo conformation or oligomerization.
source: Hh binding to Ptc leads to Smo activation in a process that involves Smo phosphorylation by PKA, CK1, and G-protein-coupled receptor kinase 2 (Gprk2), Smo accumulation at the plasma membrane and a change in Smo conformation or oligomerization (Kalderon, 2008; Maier et al., 2014; Zhao et al., 2007).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to published literature.

claim: Smo activation enhances and likely alters the nature of binding of Smo to Cos2-Fu complexes.
source: Activation enhances and likely alters the nature of binding of Smo to Cos2-Fu complexes, with two important consequences.
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge about Smo activation effects.

claim: Ci-155 processing is inhibited due to titration of Cos2 complexes away from Ci-155.
source: First, Ci-155 processing is inhibited, due to titration of Cos2 complexes away from Ci-155 and perhaps also to partial dissociation of PKA, CK1 or GSK3 from Cos2/Fu complexes (Li et al., 2014; Ranieri et al., 2014; Zhang et al., 2005).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to published literature.

claim: Cos2-associated Fu molecules are brought together to cross-phosphorylate activation loop residues, leading to full activation of Fu protein kinase activity.
source: Second, Cos2-associated Fu molecules are brought together to cross-phosphorylate activation loop residues, leading to full activation of Fu protein kinase activity (Shi et al., 2011; Zhang et al., 2011; Zhou and Kalderon, 2011).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to published literature.

claim: Activated Fu protein kinase is critical for the full activation of Ci-155.
source: Activated Fu protein kinase is critical for the full activation of Ci-155.
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge about Fu's role in Ci activation.

claim: If Ci-155 processing is blocked but there is no Fu kinase activity, Ci-155 is largely maintained in an inactive cytoplasmic form through direct associations with Suppressor of fused (Su(fu)) and Cos2.
source: If Ci-155 processing is blocked but there is no Fu kinase activity, Ci-155 is largely maintained in an inactive cytoplasmic form through direct associations with Suppressor of fused (Su(fu)) and Cos2 (Forbes et al., 1993; Ohlmeyer and Kalderon, 1998; Préat et al., 1993).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to published literature.

claim: Fu protein associations, but not kinase activity, are required for Ci-155 processing.
source: Fu protein associations, but not kinase activity, are required for Ci-155 processing; the role of Fu kinase activity in Ci-155 activation is therefore generally studied in isolation by using point mutations in the kinase domain that only eliminate protein kinase activity and reduce Ci-155 activation (Thérond et al., 1996; Zadorozny et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Ci-155 levels peak near the middle of the AP border region and decline substantially over the posterior half where Hh target gene activation is strongest.
source: However, Ci-155 levels actually peak near the middle of the AP border region and decline substantially over the posterior half where Hh target gene activation is strongest (Ohlmeyer and Kalderon, 1998; Strigini and Cohen, 1997).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: The decline in Ci-155 levels is dependent on high pathway activity and is absent in wing discs lacking Fu kinase activity.
source: This decline is dependent on high pathway activity and is absent, for example, in wing discs lacking Fu kinase activity (Ohlmeyer and Kalderon, 1998).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: The decline in Ci-155 levels has generally been attributed to the transcriptional induction of Roadkill (Rdx), also known as Hedgehog-induced BTB protein (Hib).
source: The decline in Ci-155 levels has generally been attributed to the transcriptional induction of Roadkill (Rdx), also known as Hedgehog-induced BTB protein (Hib), the substrate recognition component of a Cul3 ubiquitin ligase, culminating in the complete proteolytic destruction of ubiquitinylated Ci-155 (Jiang, 2006; Kent et al., 2006; Zhang et al., 2006).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to published literature.

claim: Loss of Rdx/Hib was initially reported to increase Ci-155 levels at the AP border.
source: Loss of Rdx/Hib was initially reported to increase Ci-155 levels at the AP border (Kent et al., 2006; Zhang et al., 2006) and Rdx/Hib can target Ci-155 directly (Zhang et al., 2009).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Rdx/Hib can target Ci-155 directly.
source: Loss of Rdx/Hib was initially reported to increase Ci-155 levels at the AP border (Kent et al., 2006; Zhang et al., 2006) and Rdx/Hib can target Ci-155 directly (Zhang et al., 2009).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: Later studies reported that Rdx/Hib can affect Ci-155 indirectly by modulating Su(fu) levels.
source: However, later studies reported that Rdx/Hib can also affect Ci-155 indirectly by modulating Su(fu) levels (Liu et al., 2014) and provided evidence that Ci-155 levels in the posterior half of the AP border of wing discs remained low in null Rdx/Hib mutant clones (Seong et al., 2010).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Ci-155 levels in the posterior half of the AP border of wing discs remained low in null Rdx/Hib mutant clones.
source: However, later studies reported that Rdx/Hib can also affect Ci-155 indirectly by modulating Su(fu) levels (Liu et al., 2014) and provided evidence that Ci-155 levels in the posterior half of the AP border of wing discs remained low in null Rdx/Hib mutant clones (Seong et al., 2010).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: The simple idea that Rdx/Hib-induced Ci-155 degradation serves to limit pathway activity in wing discs has only limited and mixed support.
source: Moreover, the simple idea that Rdx/Hib-induced Ci-155 degradation serves to limit pathway activity in wing discs has only limited and mixed support (Kent et al., 2006; Seong et al., 2010; Seong and Ishii, 2013; Zhang et al., 2006).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to published literature.

claim: Individual target genes have different sensitivities to Ci repressor and activator depending on the arrangement of Ci binding sites and the tonic influence of other transcription factors.
source: However, individual target genes have different sensitivities to Ci repressor and activator depending on the arrangement of Ci binding sites and the tonic influence of other transcription factors (Biehs et al., 2010; Méthot and Basler, 2001; Müller and Basler, 2000; Parker et al., 2011).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to published literature.

claim: Repression by Ci is essential to silence dpp but not ptc or en in anterior cells away from the wing disc AP border.
source: For example, repression by Ci is essential to silence dpp but not ptc or en in anterior cells away from the wing disc AP border.
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge about Ci repressor function.

claim: Ci-155 activation cannot be studied reliably using non-physiological levels of GAL4-responsive UAS-driven transgene expression.
source: However, we previously found that Ci-155 activation, in contrast to Ci-155 processing, cannot be studied reliably in this way (Garcia-Garcia et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to the authors' previous work.

claim: ci-null animals are very rarely rescued to adulthood using different combinations of ci-Gal4 and UAS-Ci transgenes at a variety of temperatures.
source: Specifically, ci-null animals are very rarely rescued to adulthood using different combinations of ci-Gal4 and UAS-Ci transgenes at a variety of temperatures, and anterior En expression at the AP border was not rescued in ci-null clones by UAS-Ci expressed with the commonly used wing disc driver C765-Gal4, with transgene expression alone sometimes eliciting a dominant-negative effect on Hh target gene expression (Garcia-Garcia et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to the authors' previous work.

claim: Anterior En expression at the AP border was not rescued in ci-null clones by UAS-Ci expressed with the commonly used wing disc driver C765-Gal4.
source: Specifically, ci-null animals are very rarely rescued to adulthood using different combinations of ci-Gal4 and UAS-Ci transgenes at a variety of temperatures, and anterior En expression at the AP border was not rescued in ci-null clones by UAS-Ci expressed with the commonly used wing disc driver C765-Gal4, with transgene expression alone sometimes eliciting a dominant-negative effect on Hh target gene expression (Garcia-Garcia et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to the authors' previous work.

claim: A gCi-WT transgene was readily able to rescue homozygous ci null (ci94) animals to adulthood, with normal morphology.
source: A gCi-WT transgene was readily able to rescue homozygous ci null (ci94) animals to adulthood, with normal morphology, and behaved almost like a normal ci allele but with marginally lower ci expression and activity in wing discs (Figure 1C,G).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the study, supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1.

claim: A single copy of crCi-WT in combination with ci94 resulted in efficient development of normal adults.
source: A single copy of crCi-WT in combination with ci94 resulted in efficient development of normal adults and larval wing discs with normal patterns of En, ptc-lacZ and Ci-155 expression in the anterior compartment (Figure 1D,H).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the study, supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1.

claim: Low levels of ptc-lacZ product were detected sporadically in posterior cells of wing discs when there was a single ci94 allele.
source: During these studies, we also became aware of an artifact, whereby low levels of ptc-lacZ product were detected sporadically in posterior cells of wing discs when there was a single ci94allele; this occurred in flies with a normal ci allele (on the Dp(y+) 'balancer') (Figure 1E) or with the crCi-WT allele (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is an observation from the study, supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1.

claim: PKA phosphorylates Ci-155 at amino acids S838, S856, and S892 to create recognition sites for both GSK3 and CK1.
source: PKA phosphorylates Ci-155 at amino acids S838, S856, and S892 to create recognition sites for both GSK3 and CK1, which further phosphorylate Ci-155 at a consecutive series of primed phosphorylation sites (Smelkinson and Kalderon, 2006; Smelkinson et al., 2007).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: The phosphorylation series creates a binding site for Slimb that includes the core peptide pSpTYYGpS849MQpS, spanning residues 844–852.
source: The phosphorylation series creates a binding site for Slimb that includes the core peptide pSpTYYGpS849MQpS, spanning residues 844–852.
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge about the Slimb binding site.

claim: Ci-S849A lacks the last CK1 target site initially primed by PKA phosphorylation of S838.
source: Ci-S849A lacks the last CK1 target site initially primed by PKA phosphorylation of S838 and Ci-P(1-3)A has alterations to all three PKA sites (S838A, S856A, and S892A).
evidence: This is a description of the Ci variants created for the study.

claim: Ci-P(1-3)A has alterations to all three PKA sites (S838A, S856A, and S892A).
source: Ci-S849A lacks the last CK1 target site initially primed by PKA phosphorylation of S838 and Ci-P(1-3)A has alterations to all three PKA sites (S838A, S856A, and S892A).
evidence: This is a description of the Ci variants created for the study.

claim: Ci fragments with S849A or P(1-3)A alterations showed complete loss of Slimb binding in vitro after phosphorylation by PKA, CK1 and GSK3.
source: Ci fragments with those alterations showed complete loss of Slimb binding in vitro after phosphorylation by PKA, CK1 and GSK3, while UAS-Ci transgene products with those changes showed no processing in wing discs, judged by a sensitive assay of repressor function in posterior compartment wing disc cells (Smelkinson and Kalderon, 2006; Smelkinson et al., 2007).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: UAS-Ci transgene products with S849A or P(1-3)A alterations showed no processing in wing discs.
source: Ci fragments with those alterations showed complete loss of Slimb binding in vitro after phosphorylation by PKA, CK1 and GSK3, while UAS-Ci transgene products with those changes showed no processing in wing discs, judged by a sensitive assay of repressor function in posterior compartment wing disc cells (Smelkinson and Kalderon, 2006; Smelkinson et al., 2007).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Wing discs of animals with crCi-S849A or crCi-P(1-3)A in combination with ci94 had expanded anterior regions.
source: The wing discs of animals with crCi-S849A or crCi-P(1-3)A in combination with ci94 had expanded anterior regions (Figure 2A–D), as expected because Ci-75 repressor, normally produced from Ci-155 processing, is required to silence dpp expression in anterior cells and ectopic anterior Dpp induces anterior growth (Méthot and Basler, 1999).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the study, supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2.

claim: Wing discs with crCi-S849A or crCi-P(1-3)A had strongly elevated Ci-155 levels throughout the anterior.
source: We also found that these wing discs had strongly elevated Ci-155 levels throughout the anterior, indicating that full-length Ci-155 was not being processed in the absence of the Hh signal, as expected (Figure 2A–D; Figure 2—figure supplement 1A–D,G,H).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the study, supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2.

claim: The Hh-stimulated decline in Ci-155 levels begins at a location where ptc-lacZ induction is roughly half-maximal and is roughly linear, resulting in a reduction of over twofold by the compartment boundary.
source: The Hh-stimulated decline in Ci-155 levels begins at a location where ptc-lacZ induction is roughly half-maximal and is roughly linear, resulting in a reduction of over twofold by the compartment boundary (Figure 2H", I", K; Figure 8).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the study, supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2 and Figure 8.

claim: The inhibition of Ci-155 processing extended from a location slightly anterior to the edge of ptc-lacZ induction to the AP border in a clearly graded manner that would alter Ci-155 levels more than two-fold.
source: The inhibition of Ci-155 processing extended from a location slightly anterior to the edge of ptc-lacZ induction to the AP border in a clearly graded manner that, in isolation, would alter Ci-155 levels more than two-fold.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental data analyzing Ci-155 profiles.

claim: Ci-S3-5 supported a normal pattern of Hh target gene induction in wing discs and the development of adults with normal wings.
source: This Ci variant (Ci-S3-5) supported a normal pattern of Hh target gene induction in wing discs and the development of adults with normal wings.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the study, supported by experimental data.

claim: The Ci-155 profile for Ci-S3-5 was very similar to wild-type Ci with robust Hh-stimulated Ci-155 reduction in the posterior part of the AP border.
source: The Ci-155 profile was also very similar to wild-type Ci with robust Hh-stimulated Ci-155 reduction in the posterior part of the AP border.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the study, supported by experimental data.

claim: The majority of Hh-promoted Ci-155 reduction is through mechanisms other than degradation due to direct binding of Rdx/Hib.
source: While the Ci variant may retain some residual Hib binding, our results suggest that the majority of Hh-promoted Ci-155 reduction is through mechanisms other than degradation due to direct binding of Rdx/Hib.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental data with Ci-S3-5.

claim: The complete absence of Su(fu) greatly reduces Ci-155 levels but not ci RNA levels throughout wing discs.
source: The complete absence of Su(fu) greatly reduces Ci-155 levels but not ci RNA levels throughout wing discs (Ohlmeyer and Kalderon, 1998), leading to the hypothesis that direct binding of Su(fu) to Ci-155 protects Ci-155 from degradation.
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: Direct binding of Su(fu) to Ci-155 protects Ci-155 from degradation.
source: The complete absence of Su(fu) greatly reduces Ci-155 levels but not ci RNA levels throughout wing discs (Ohlmeyer and Kalderon, 1998), leading to the hypothesis that direct binding of Su(fu) to Ci-155 protects Ci-155 from degradation.
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on cited literature.

claim: No reduction of Ci-155 levels close to the source of Hh was apparent in wing discs lacking Su(fu).
source: Consistent with this hypothesis, no reduction of Ci-155 levels close to the source of Hh was apparent in wing discs lacking Su(fu).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the study, supported by experimental data.

claim: Artificially activated Fu (GAP-Fu) can activate processing-resistant Ci in anterior, Hh-free territory as effectively as normal Fu activity at the AP border.
source: We found that artificially activated Fu (GAP-Fu) can activate processing-resistant Ci in anterior, Hh-free territory as effectively as normal Fu activity at the AP border.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the study, supported by experimental data.

claim: Wild-type Ci activated by GAP-Fu induced roughly two-fold lower levels of ptc-lacZ than processing-resistant Ci variants.
source: Wild-type Ci activated by GAP-Fu induced roughly two-fold lower levels of ptc-lacZ, and barely induced ptc-lacZ at all if it was produced at slightly lower levels by a gCi transgene rather than a ci allele.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the study, supported by experimental data.

claim: The steady-state level of Ci-155 in cells with synthetically activated Fu was not significantly higher for processing-resistant variants than for wild-type Ci.
source: However, the steady-state level of Ci-155 in cells with synthetically activated Fu was not significantly higher for processing-resistant variants than for wild-type Ci, presumably because of robust Ci-155 degradation in response to high pathway activity.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the study, supported by experimental data.

claim: High pathway activity causes a high rate of Ci-155 loss.
source: The GAP-Fu experiment reports that high pathway activity causes a high rate of Ci-155 loss and that high pathway activity can only be maintained if there is an adequate, constant supply of fresh Ci-155 protected from processing.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental data with GAP-Fu.

claim: High pathway activity can only be maintained if there is an adequate, constant supply of fresh Ci-155 protected from processing.
source: The GAP-Fu experiment reports that high pathway activity causes a high rate of Ci-155 loss and that high pathway activity can only be maintained if there is an adequate, constant supply of fresh Ci-155 protected from processing.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental data with GAP-Fu.

claim: Genetic removal of PKA substantially increased Ci-155 activity in the absence of Hh when using processing-deficient variant Ci-P(1-3A).
source: We used the processing-deficient variant Ci-P(1-3A) to show that genetic removal of PKA or Cos2 substantially increased Ci-155 activity in the absence of Hh, providing evidence that both PKA and Cos2 inhibit Ci-155 activation in addition to their well-established roles of promoting Ci-155 processing (Figure 8).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the study, supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8.

claim: Genetic removal of Cos2 substantially increased Ci-155 activity in the absence of Hh when using processing-deficient variant Ci-P(1-3A).
source: We used the processing-deficient variant Ci-P(1-3A) to show that genetic removal of PKA or Cos2 substantially increased Ci-155 activity in the absence of Hh, providing evidence that both PKA and Cos2 inhibit Ci-155 activation in addition to their well-established roles of promoting Ci-155 processing (Figure 8).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the study, supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8.

claim: Removal of the CORD domain of Ci conferred significantly higher activity on a processing-resistant Ci variant.
source: We found that removal of the CORD domain of Ci conferred significantly higher activity on a processing-resistant Ci variant and increased the response of otherwise normal Ci to loss of PKA, but not to loss of Cos2.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the study, supported by experimental data.

claim: Removal of the CORD domain increased the response of otherwise normal Ci to loss of PKA, but not to loss of Cos2.
source: We found that removal of the CORD domain of Ci conferred significantly higher activity on a processing-resistant Ci variant and increased the response of otherwise normal Ci to loss of PKA, but not to loss of Cos2.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the study, supported by experimental data.

claim: The CORD domain is the major mediator of the inhibitory action of Cos2.
source: These observations are consistent with the hypothesis that the CORD domain is the major mediator of the inhibitory action of Cos2.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental data on CORD domain deletions.

claim: Deletion of the CDN Cos2-binding domain did not alter the activity of processing-resistant Ci.
source: By contrast, deletion of the CDN Cos2-binding domain did not alter the activity of processing-resistant Ci.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the study, supported by experimental data.

claim: Ci-155 processing remained efficient in the absence of both CDN and CORD domains.
source: Ci-155 processing remained efficient in the absence of both CDN and CORD domains, confirming a previous deduction from UAS-Ci transgenes that Cos2 binding to the zinc finger domain of Ci can suffice to promote processing (Zhou and Kalderon, 2011).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the study, supported by experimental data and a citation to previous work.

claim: Removal of the CORD domain reduced En induction at the AP border.
source: Removal of the CORD domain reduced En induction at the AP border and we hypothesize that this might result from a deficiency in targeting activated Fu to Ci.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the study, supported by experimental data.

claim: Loss of PKA increased the activity of Ci-P(1-3A), showing that the PKA sites used to direct processing (P1-3) are not essential targets for PKA to inhibit Ci-155.
source: The finding that loss of PKA increased the activity of Ci-P(1-3A) shows that the PKA sites used to direct processing (P1-3) are not essential targets for PKA to inhibit Ci-155.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental data with Ci-P(1-3A).

claim: At the AP border of wing discs, Hh inhibits Ci-155 processing, activates full-length Ci-155 and promotes reduction of Ci-155, most likely substantially through proteolytic degradation.
source: In summary, at the AP border of wing discs, Hh inhibits Ci-155 processing, activates full-length Ci-155 and promotes reduction of Ci-155, most likely substantially through proteolytic degradation (Figure 8).
evidence: This is a summary conclusion from the study, supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8.

claim: Hh can pattern wing discs and wings normally in the absence of regulated processing.
source: Processing-resistant Ci variants revealed the profiles of Hh-promoted Ci-155 reduction and Ci-155 processing inhibition (Figure 2K,L and Figure 8), and showed that Hh can pattern wing discs and wings normally in the absence of regulated processing.
evidence: This is a primary conclusion from the study, supported by experimental data shown in Figures 2 and 8.

claim: Ci-155 reduction likely depends on Hh-stimulated processes other than direct binding to the transcriptionally induced component of an E3 ubiquitin ligase.
source: Ci variants lacking Rdx/Hib-binding sites showed that Ci-155 reduction likely depends on Hh-stimulated processes other than direct binding to the transcriptionally induced component of an E3 ubiquitin ligase, plausibly involving protection from degradation by Su(fu) association (Figure 8).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental data with Ci-S3-5, shown in Figure 8.

claim: Ci-155 that is not subject to processing is substantially inhibited by PKA and by association with Cos2 through the CORD domain in addition to Su(fu).
source: We also found that Ci-155 that is not subject to processing is substantially inhibited by PKA and by association with Cos2 through the CORD domain in addition to Su(fu), and that activation by Fu only elicits strong induction of Hh target genes if there is a continued ample supply of Ci-155 protected from processing.
evidence: This is a primary conclusion from the study, supported by experimental data.

claim: Activation by Fu only elicits strong induction of Hh target genes if there is a continued ample supply of Ci-155 protected from processing.
source: We also found that Ci-155 that is not subject to processing is substantially inhibited by PKA and by association with Cos2 through the CORD domain in addition to Su(fu), and that activation by Fu only elicits strong induction of Hh target genes if there is a continued ample supply of Ci-155 protected from processing.
evidence: This is a primary conclusion from the study, supported by experimental data.
